clue.text: Not half common and grasping, grasping book that may be grasped

indicators.note: only the first half of the word common is kept, the rest is discarded
the second grasping means holding something inside, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: prehensile describes a tail or limb able to grasp

explanation.surface: A rather vulgar, greedy reader clutching a volume that can be held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grasping' appears twice with two jobs: first as a synonym for prehensile, then, after the comma, as the container signal. 'Not half' means keep the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comprehensible can be understood, and to grasp an idea is to understand it.

clue.text: Misguidedly anoint camel with oil as itch-relief treatment

indicators.note: acting misguidedly means going wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly rubs oil on a camel as a remedy for itching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misguidedly' rearranges ANOINT CAMEL and OIL; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink zinc-based lotion is a familiar soothing remedy for sunburn and itchy skin.

clue.text: Seaman Silas circumnavigates Italy

indicators.note: to circumnavigate is to go all the way round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: Silas Marner is the weaver in George Eliot's novel
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A sailor called Silas sails right round Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a sailor, a person who works at sea.

clue.text: Torturer receiving support from extortionist

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so the support goes inside the torturer

parts.note: a racker is one who stretches victims on the rack
a tee supports a golf ball before it is struck

explanation.surface: A torturer is paid off by a man running a protection racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs a criminal racket, typically extorting money by threats.

clue.text: Bearing on underworld (Greek)

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: hell is the underworld of the damned
ENE, east-north-east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A remark about the underworld, bracketed as Greek mythology.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'on' puts ENE below HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek, from Hellas, the Greeks' own name for Greece.

clue.text: Concerning intersections and loci, maybe

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged otherwise, so they are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A mathematical note about points where lines cross and sets of points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges AND LOCI; the surface pretends loci is an example of intersections.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodical means relating to nodes, the points where curves or orbits cross.

clue.text: Supply inspiration that's taking graduate to university

indicators.note: taking means holding inside, so i.e. surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: that's, meaning that is, is i.e. (id est)
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a graduate's degree

explanation.surface: Something inspiring happens when a graduate is sent off to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' splits the abbreviation i.e. around the degree and university letters; 'Supply inspiration' together is the verb definition, not 'inspiration' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue is to fill or inspire someone with a feeling or quality.

clue.text: US city rules out poet's crown

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American city bans the garland of poetic honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'rules out' poses as 'bans', but the word rules is shuffled after the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath of laurel leaves was the crown given to poets in antiquity.

clue.text: Flowers keeping warm, last of light shines out — it makes the garden grow

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the flowers surround warm

parts.note: a posy is a small bunch of flowers
hot means very warm

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are turned out of their order
last of picks out the final letter of light

explanation.surface: Sunlit blooms flourish as the light fades, with a hint of how gardens thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts warm inside the bunch of flowers; 'out' shuffles the final letter of light, from 'last of', together with shines.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants make their food from light through this process, which is what lets them grow.

clue.text: Sweet-sounding, moving heart of Julian Clary?

indicators.note: moving means changing position, so the letters are rearranged
the heart of a word is its central letters, here of Julian

explanation.surface: Is the core of the camp comedian Julian Clary melodious and touching?
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes LI from JULIAN; 'moving' rearranges LI and CLARY. Julian Clary is a British comedian and entertainer; 'moving' poses as 'emotionally stirring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical means songlike and melodious, as lyrics are written to be sung.

clue.text: Corrupt H3 taking a turn?

indicators.note: taking means holding something inside, so A goes in
turn means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: H with a superscript 3 is H cubed

explanation.surface: Could the chemical H3 be corrupted by being made to spin?
explanation.walkthrough: Read H3 aloud as H CUBED; 'turn' reverses it to DEBUCH and 'taking' puts A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To debauch someone is to corrupt them morally, leading them into excess.

clue.text: Home to minister with fine head of hair concealing silver root

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the root of silver goes within

parts.note: a mane is a long, flowing head of hair

indicators.note: the root of a word is where it begins, its first letter

explanation.surface: A clergyman with luxuriant locks hides grey showing at the roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' puts S, from 'silver root', inside MANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is the house provided for a minister, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Waste old money securing rock group

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so the money encloses the group

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
REM was an American rock band

explanation.surface: An outdated sum of cash is wasted on hiring a rock band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' means the money holds the band inside it. 'Waste' looks like a verb but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Excrement is bodily waste matter discharged from the bowels.

clue.text: Spooner's to wait on Eleanor with transmitter

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the starts of words, so the initial sounds trade places

parts.note: to wait on someone is to serve them
Nell is a pet form of Eleanor

explanation.surface: A clergyman offers to attend Eleanor, who has a radio set.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron carries and passes on nerve impulses, so it transmits signals.

clue.text: Fish one consumed in foundation

indicators.note: consumed in means swallowed inside, so one goes inside the fish

parts.note: a bass is a fish
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fish is eaten as the base of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the foundation or underlying support on which something rests.

clue.text: Boycotts drug in dangerous location

parts.note: to black goods or a firm is to boycott them, a trade-union term
pot is cannabis

explanation.surface: Unions refuse to handle drugs in a hazardous place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blacks' meaning boycotts is British trade-union usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A black spot is a place where accidents or trouble often happen.

clue.text: Terminator's head blown off by tail-ender

indicators.note: having its head blown off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a closer is one who ends or terminates something

explanation.surface: The Terminator gets his head blown off by the last man in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head blown off' drops C from CLOSER. A tail-ender is a weak batsman at the bottom of a cricket order, and the one who comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A tail-ender comes last, as does the loser of a race.

clue.text: High quality drinks on the rocks served up?

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters read from bottom to top
a drink on the rocks has ice in it, so the ice goes inside

parts.note: an animal drinks by lapping, so laps means drinks
the rocks is slang for ice in a drink

explanation.surface: Fine spirits poured over ice and brought to the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' works because a drink on the rocks contains ice; 'served up' reverses the whole in this down entry, reading bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Special means exceptional or of superior quality.

clue.text: Daft pictures being displayed in burgh

parts.note: dumb means stupid or daft
art means pictures or paintings
on means being shown, as a film is on

explanation.surface: Silly pictures are on show in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: A burgh is a Scottish town with a charter; Dumbarton is one, west of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbarton is a royal burgh, an example of the Scottish chartered town.

clue.text: Taking action about director general's evasive behaviour

indicators.note: about means around, so the action surrounds the initials

parts.note: doing means taking action
DG is the abbreviation for director general

explanation.surface: Acting to deal with the boss's slippery conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodging means evading, avoiding something by quick or shifty moves.

clue.text: Alcoholic measure to butter up composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means all the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a unit is the UK's standard measure of alcohol
a ram butts, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A tot of spirits is used to flatter a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses UNIT and RAM to MAR-TINU; 'butter up' looks like flattery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohuslav Martinu was a twentieth-century Czech composer.

clue.text: Troops occupying shipshape Oriental ship

indicators.note: occupying means filling a space within, so the troops go inside

parts.note: trim means neat and shipshape
RE, the Royal Engineers, are troops
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Soldiers take over a tidy Eastern vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts the Royal Engineers inside the tidy word; 'Oriental' adds east at the end. A trireme is a classical galley.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient warship with three banks of oars.

clue.text: Month implausibly mired in divinity

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shuffled letters go inside the god

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

indicators.note: implausibly suggests an unlikely arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A month implausibly stuck in religious studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implausibly' shuffles mired, and 'in' places that inside the Norse god. The month comes from the calendar of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermidor was the eleventh month of the French Revolutionary calendar, in summer.

clue.text: Bohemian taking in a coastal city

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so A goes inside

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's opera La Boheme

explanation.surface: An unconventional artist takes in a seaside city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bohemian' looks like 'unconventional person' but points at the opera's Mimi.
explanation.definitionFit: Miami is a city on the Atlantic coast of Florida.

clue.text: Kosher nibbles Isaac sometimes had for starters?

definitions.text: Kosher nibbles Isaac sometimes had for starters?

indicators.note: starters are the beginnings, so the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: Isaac occasionally ate a kosher snack as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes the first letters of five words; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A knish is a Jewish dough snack, often eaten as a starter or nibble.

clue.text: Paperwork enabling state to enter final state, retrospectively

indicators.note: to enter means going inside, so one piece goes within the other
retrospectively means looking back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the imago is the final adult stage of an insect
RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Documents allow a nation to reach its ultimate condition, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' turns only the insect stage backwards; 'to enter' then sets the Rhode Island abbreviation inside it, after its first letter. 'enabling' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the art of folding paper, so it is literally paper work.

clue.text: Stamp around 1,000 spires

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters about into a new order

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1,000

explanation.surface: A seal surrounds a thousand church spires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges M and SPIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to stamp a mark or design into a surface.

clue.text: Supporter, knowing way in, pinches bottom

parts.note: fly is British slang for knowing or sharp

indicators.note: pinches means holding tight inside, so the bottom goes within

parts.note: ingress means a way in or entrance
butt is slang for bottom

explanation.surface: A knowing fan slips in and pinches someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinches' sets the bottom inside the entrance word. 'Supporter' looks like a fan, but it is an architectural prop; fly meaning knowing is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying buttress is an arched support propping up a wall, as on Gothic churches.
